To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of a sex chromosome in females triggers a sex-specific transcriptional response in the female reproductive tissue, and that the Y chromosome exerts an impact on the transcriptome of somatic tissues shared between males and females.
the Y chromosome is a hotspot for sex specific adaptation and genomic responses in female reproductive and neuronal tissues.
the Y chromosome exerts sex-specific effects in female reproductive and larval neuronal tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the Y chromosome on gene expression and phenotypic variation.
the role of Y chromosomes in the evolution of sex-specific traits and the genetic basis of sexual dimorphism.
the impact of Y chromosomes in the soma and reproductive tissues of females.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the Y chromosome is a major determinant for gene regulation and expression in both sexes.
Y-linked genes and Y-linked genetic elements are under selection in the somatic tissues shared between males and females and in reproductive tissue, and that this selection is sex-specific.
Y-linked genes are not just junk, and they have an impact in a wide range of tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Y chromosome presence in females induces a sex-biased response in reproductive and neuronal tissues.
the Y chromosome, in the presence of an X chromosome, is a hotspot for sex determination, sex-specific adaptation, as well as somatically active genes.
the presence of the Y chromosome in females induces a disproportionate response in the ovaries and the nervous system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to its role in male fertility, the Y chromosome may also be important for female reproduction.
the Y chromosome has a much larger impact on the transcriptome of female reproductive and neuronal tissues compared to male reproductive and neuronal tissues.
Y-linked genes are under selection and that the Y chromosome is a hotspot for sex specific adaptation.
